title: Sonic the Hedgehog: Triple Trouble
subtitle: Three rivals for the emeralds
summary: Sonic the Hedgehog: Triple Trouble is Aspect's platform game, first released for Game Gear in Japan on 11 November 1994.
body: Sonic the Hedgehog: Triple Trouble is Aspect's platform game, first released for Game Gear in Japan on 11 November 1994. Sonic and Tails try to protect the Chaos Emeralds from Doctor Robotnik, Knuckles and the treasure hunter Fang, known internationally as Nack. Six zones carry the adventure through familiar running, jumping and boss encounters, with a choice between the two heroes. The handheld sequel builds on Sonic Chaos while giving each protagonist particular movement and equipment, allowing the same overall journey to produce different opportunities inside its stages.

Both Sonic and Tails can use a spin dash to accelerate from a stationary roll. Sonic also has the peel-out move associated with Sonic CD, while Tails can fly for a limited time. Those abilities encourage different approaches to platforms and gaps: a useful run-up may favour Sonic, while an elevated opening can reward Tails' flight. Each zone ends with a boss after its opening stages, giving the route a repeated progression from learning the environment to facing a more concentrated mechanical challenge at the end.

Some power-ups belong to only one hero, including Sonic's jet board and equipment for Tails' underwater travel. Collecting them can change how a section is crossed, making the choice of character visible in the route as well as the animation. Yayoi Fujimori composed the music. Fang's introduction also added another recurring face to the wider series. Triple Trouble gives the Game Gear its own substantial Sonic journey, using the two heroes' abilities and colourful stages to bring the handheld adventure closer to the variety associated with the larger console games.
